correctness.rationale: The edge-restricted heat operators have positive spectra, and a Sylvester integral identity exactly evaluates their Frobenius trajectory error. Exact symbolic rational comparison on every positive-weight triangle factors each edge-deletion error difference as the conductance difference times a rational function with strictly positive numerator and denominator coefficients. Triangle edge permutations yield all comparisons. Four-cycle errors are exact rational values and strictly ordered; standalone symbolic checker was run successfully on actual files. No stochastic or finite simulation is used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Choosing a single removable edge under a fixed budget is a natural decision in graph heat-flow reduction. A positive universal guarantee on every triangle, paired with a rigorously smallest four-cycle reversal, identifies where an appealing conductance-only heuristic loses validity for full-time trajectory fidelity. This nonmonotone threshold is a structural boundary, not an arbitrary numerical benchmark.
